title: Time-Bound Verbal Drills
tagline: Year 4 — Quick verbal items under 30 seconds: synonyms, antonyms, one-word substitutes, fill-blanks and error spotting

introduction.overview: Quick verbal items (a synonym, an antonym, a one-word substitute, a fill-blank, a simple error) should take 20–30 seconds each. They reward vocabulary and grammar knowledge and cost little time, so they should be answered first in any timed section. This chapter is a drill of such items, with a pacing method: answer what you know at once, mark doubtful items, and leave long passages for last.
introduction.placementRelevance: Online verbal sections often open with such quick items; speed here buys time for passages.
introduction.realWorldContext: Quick, accurate language checks are part of everyday writing.

learningObjectives: Answer quick items in under 30 seconds
Use grammar rules for instant fixes
Budget time between quick items and passages

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: If you do not know a word, use its root or the sentence; if still unsure, eliminate and guess.

coreDefinitions: Quick item: answered in under 30 seconds.
Elimination: removing options you know are wrong.
Mark and skip: leaving a doubtful item for later.
One-word substitute: a single word for a phrase.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Know-it-or-not decisions should take seconds; spend the saved time on passages.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Read, decide, mark, move. Do not agonise over words you do not know.

mainNarrative: A section with 10 quick items should take about 5 minutes. If you spend two minutes on one word, you lose three quick items.
Use roots: "fearless" is without fear; "dishonest" is not honest.
One-word substitutes: a person who walks in sleep is a somnambulist; a fear of heights is acrophobia.
For grammar, use the rule: each is singular, so "each of the students was".
Mark doubtful items and return only if time remains.

deepDiveAspects.title: Elimination odds
deepDiveAspects.content: Removing two options doubles the chance of a correct guess.

deepDiveAspects.title: Do not over-think
deepDiveAspects.content: Easy items answered fast leave time for harder ones.

solvedExamples.title: Time budget
solvedExamples.question: You plan 10 quick items at 30 seconds each. How long is that?

solvedExamples.title: Elimination
solvedExamples.question: You can remove two of four options. What is the chance of guessing correctly?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Answer at once, eliminate if unsure, mark and move on; spend the saved time on passages.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate the two most obviously wrong options first.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Accuracy on quick items is mostly vocabulary built over time.

easy.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "brief".
easy.explanation: Brief means lasting a short time.

easy.explanation: The prefix dis- reverses the meaning.
